sections.subtitle: Current Form and Team News
sections.text: Aston Villa, sitting in 4th place with 51 points, have had a mixed run in their last five matches, securing two wins and suffering three losses. West Ham United, languishing in 18th with 29 points, show signs of improvement with an unbeaten streak in their last three games, including a draw against Manchester City. Both teams will miss key players, with Villa without Boubacar Kamara and West Ham missing Crysencio Summerville, which could impact their midfield creativity.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-Head Record
sections.text: In their last two encounters, Aston Villa have had the upper hand, winning one and drawing the other, maintaining an unbeaten run against West Ham over seven matches. Historical data indicates both teams often score in these fixtures, suggesting a competitive clash at Villa Park.

sections.subtitle: Key Players to Watch
sections.text: Aston Villa’s Morgan Rogers has been a standout performer against West Ham, consistently delivering impactful performances. For West Ham, Jarrod Bowen is in fine form, contributing crucial goals and assists in recent matches, making him a significant threat.

sections.subtitle: Tactical Outlook
sections.text: Villa’s strong possession stats and ability to create chances in the final third could dominate the game, especially at home. West Ham’s resilience and knack for late goals might push them to exploit any defensive lapses, particularly on the counter.

sections.subtitle: Match Expectations
sections.text: Given Aston Villa’s superior league position and home advantage, they are favored to take the win, aligning with Sofascore’s 53% probability for a home victory. However, West Ham’s recent form suggests they won’t go down easily, and the 55% chance of both teams scoring indicates an open game.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Half-time overview
halftimeSections.text: At half-time, Aston Villa leads West Ham United 1-0 at Villa Park. The home side has dominated much of the game, controlling possession and creating several scoring opportunities. John McGinn's goal in the 15th minute has given Villa the edge, capitalizing on their attacking intent early in the match. West Ham, on the other hand, has struggled to make an impact in the final third, failing to register a shot on target in the first half. The Hammers will need to regroup if they are to turn this game around.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Aston Villa's dominance
halftimeSections.text: Aston Villa has been the superior side in almost every department. Their control of the ball and frequent entries into the final third have kept West Ham on the back foot. The home team has created multiple big chances, though they've missed a couple of key opportunities to extend their lead. Players like Jadon Sancho and Morgan Rogers have been instrumental in creating plays, while McGinn's clinical finishing has made the difference. Villa's high duel-winning rate also shows their physical edge in midfield and defense.

halftimeSections.subtitle: West Ham's struggles
halftimeSections.text: West Ham United has had a tough first half, unable to match Villa's intensity. Their limited possession and lack of penetration into the penalty area highlight their difficulties in building attacks. The Hammers have been forced into a defensive stance, with minimal success in winning duels or creating chances. A yellow card early on has also put them under slight disciplinary pressure. Without a significant tactical shift, it’s hard to see them breaking through Villa's solid structure.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: The first half saw Aston Villa consistently maintaining the upper hand in attack, with frequent spells of pressure in the opposition half, especially around the time of their goal. There were moments where West Ham tried to push back with brief attacking surges, particularly in the early minutes and towards the half-hour mark, but these efforts quickly faded. Villa regained momentum with sustained periods of dominance, showcasing their intent to control the game through relentless forward play.
